Excited to introduce Icon, The First AI Admaker.

We’re backed by Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund & execs of frontier AI labs like OpenAI, Pika, & Cognition.

Icon (http://icon.me) is like ChatGPT + CapCut, but for making winning ads with AI in minutes.

How it works:
1. Icon looks at your video library & tags scenes (e.g. "close-up," "unboxing"). These scenes become reusable clips used as lego blocks for making ads.
2. Prompt Icon’s AdGPT to generate scripts focused on specific angles & audiences.
3. Icon finds perfectly matching clips for every script scene & generates an ad that is 80-99% complete.
4. Make edits with our CapCut-like video editor until you're happy.

3-person creative teams make 30 ads per month. With Icon, they make 300.

We co-built Icon with $100M+ revenue brands like Ridge, Jones Road, Immi, Backbone, & MUD\WTR to solve big pain-points:

1. Making lots of ads is extremely painful. Icon helps you automate the tedious parts of scriptwriting, scene matching, video editing, audience research, UGC creation, & more.

2. AI-generated ads look like trash. Icon remixes your existing footage into new ads, matching your production quality & maintaining brand aesthetics.

3. Existing solutions charge $2K-$30K/month for:
🔍 Competitor ad spying & cloning
📈 Creative analytics
📹 Custom & stock avatars for AI UGC
👥 Audience research
📁 Video storage & tagging

Icon does scriptwriting & video editing on top of everything above for just $999/year (their margin is our opportunity 😉).

If you’ve made it this far, we have a surprise for you 👇🏻

I made this ad with Icon - the new viral AI ad making tool.

Here are my initial (unbiased) thoughts after playing around with it over the last few days:

- I’m honestly blown away by how many features this thing has for its’ price. A scriptwriter, editor, asset library, AI UGC, creative analytics, a spy tool and an ad uploader for $399/mo is wild.

- Impressed with the integration options. I usually use Air, but the Air integration was a little slow (I’ll chalk that up to high launch traffic). But I was able to upload my assets to GDrive and sync that way instead. Dropbox and Frame are also available. Being able to dynamically sync your entire library is huge.

- The scripts do need a bit of tweaking. Though it’s difficult to fault Icon for this - because even with Claude and GPT, it’s almost impossible to ‘one-prompt’ a good ad script. Icon’s scriptwriter is conversational, so you can give it feedback just like you would other LLMs. Either that or be prepared to tweak it manually. For this ad, I just fed it one of our own scripts that we wrote ages ago.

- The AI editor seemed to find the right broll about 60% of the time. This could’ve been higher if I had more broll (I synced 100 clips, mainly solution oriented) or if I allowed it to create AI UGC too. In this case I didn’t, because I wanted to see how good of a job it did with my existing footage. It took about 20 minutes of work inside the editor to get it from what it gave me to what you see here. Not perfect, but definitely less time than it would’ve taken manually - and I would imagine its’ clip selection will improve over time.

- They’ve clearly built this tool pretty closely with people who know creative. Lots of options for different ways to build an ad (write new script, create from existing script, copy another ad etc). Right now, you can only do broll + voiceovers. But as soon as this thing can build aroll mashups itself from your raw asset library…wow. The possibilities are endless. I’m told the beta for that is going to be available next week, so that’s something I’ll be monitoring closely.

I would love at some point to see Icon use adaptive learning through its’ connection to the ad account. Imagine if it could make an ad, see how the ad performed, and use that information to make better ads in future. Then, suddenly it becomes a very, very powerful tool.

Overall, I’m bullish on the platform. I think it has the potential to help brands dramatically increase their low production output.

I’ll continue testing over the next few days to work out how to best use Icon, then I’ll be dropping a YouTube tutorial with my findings on Tuesday/Wednesday.

And btw, I am not being paid by Icon for this post, nor do I have a stake in the company. I just like trying new tools to see if they can improve my teams’ workflow.
